🇲🇽🚆 <u>Mexico is doubling its railways — 2,377 km of new passenger and freight track</u>

Sheinbaum's government is laying 2,377 km of new rail — double what the entire previous administration built — with military engineers already about 800 km into four simultaneous corridors: AIFA–Pachuca, CDMX–Querétaro, Querétaro–Irapuato and Saltillo–Nuevo Laredo. Passenger service starts returning between November 2026 and February 2027, on the way to more than 3,000 km by 2030 — reversing decades of neoliberal dismantling of Mexico's trains.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico moves to bar dual nationals from the presidency and governorships</u>

Sheinbaum's constitutional reform amending Articles 82, 116 and 122 would stop anyone holding or acquiring a foreign nationality from becoming president, governor or Mexico City mayor — they'd have to renounce it before registering as a candidate. The stated purpose: that "el interés de México esté por encima de cualquier otro" ("Mexico's interest above any other"). Commissions take it up Sept 9, with a floor vote expected the third week of September.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>MEXICO EATS THE OIL SPIKE SO DRIVERS DON'T</u>

As global crude climbs, Mexico's Finance Ministry raised its fuel subsidy for Sept 5–11: the state now absorbs about 68% of the gasoline IEPS tax — cutting the Magna levy to 4.59 pesos a liter — and 90.78% of the diesel tax, dropping it to 0.67 pesos. That's what holds Magna under 24 pesos and diesel under 28 at the pump, absorbing the oil-price shock so consumers don't.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>TLATELOLCO PACKED TO DEFEND MEXICO'S SOVEREIGNTY</u>

Tens of thousands filled the Plaza de las Tres Culturas in Tlatelolco to close out 379 neighborhood assemblies held across Mexico City since June, defending national sovereignty and the Fourth Transformation days after Sheinbaum's second-year report. It's the same square where the state massacred students in 1968 — now filled to defend the transformation, not crushed by the regime.

🇲🇽📚 <u>UNAM OWNS ITS EXAM FAILURE, RETURNS TO IN-PERSON TESTING</u>

UNAM — Latin America's largest public university — publicly took responsibility for a botched online entrance exam after scores above 90 leapt from 5.1% in 2024 to unprecedented highs, a red flag the remote format couldn't police. Rector Leonardo Lomelí said the online exam "will not be used again until a robust and secure operational model is in place," and admissions return to in-person testing.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>DECLASSIFIED: THE CIA WEIGHED INVADING MEXICO</u>

Declassified documents show the CIA gamed out a "unilateral military intervention" in Mexico in 1989 — to be considered only "in the extremely unlikely event of imminent political system collapse" during the Salinas years, which the agency put at a 20% chance of severe economic breakdown. The same government Washington stood ready to prop up privatized some 400 state enterprises and enriched 40 families off the sale.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO TO WASHINGTON: TRADE, NOT SUBMISSION</u>

With Washington complaining about its trade deficit, Sheinbaum says Mexico is studying whether to buy more from the US "instead of buying from other countries" — a negotiation, not a concession. Meanwhile Mexican exports to the US keep breaking records, powered by electronics feeding the American AI and data-center boom.
